inspection_outcome: Verified central false lemma and dependent derivation gap; selected minor correctable issues
summary: Supremum-defined Favard spaces are not generally fractional-power domains. A self-adjoint dyadic example refutes Lemma 2.16 and its norm equivalence; the identity is explicitly used in important applications.
limitations: No counterexample to every convergence-rate conclusion or to the Coulomb rate was established.
No complete repair of general fractional-gamma corollaries was verified.
Section 3 is separate and only selectively checked.

problems.title: False Favard/fractional-domain identification

source_claim.locator: Lemma 2.16 PDF pp.22-23; Remark 2.17; Cor.2.19,2.22 and application pp.24-27
source_claim.text: F_alpha(-K)=D(K^alpha) and F_alpha(iK)=D(|K|^alpha), with equivalent norms, for self-adjoint K and all alpha>0.

assumptions: X=ell^2(N), K e_k=2^k e_k, natural self-adjoint domain
A=-K generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup and iK a unitary group

check.type: Exact analytic counterexample and finite cutoff sequence
steps: K^(1/2)x is the all-ones sequence, hence not in ell^2.
For every lambda>0, sum lambda*2^k/(lambda+2^k)^2 <=4 by splitting 2^k<=lambda and >lambda.
For iK replace denominator by lambda^2+4^k; same bound.
Truncations x^(N) have uniformly bounded Favard norm but K^(1/2) norm sqrt(N).
The proof's optimizing lambda depends on spectral variable, so supremum cannot be exchanged with integration.
check.result: Both equalities and claimed reverse norm equivalence false under all stated relevant assumptions.

counterevidence: D(K^alpha) is continuously included in F_alpha for 0<alpha<1.
For gamma=1, a direct spectral graph-domain commutator estimate yields min(beta,1-alpha) without the false identity.
No counterexample to the paper's Coulomb rate was constructed.

impact.dependency: Lemma 2.16 -> Remark 2.17 -> Corollaries 2.19/2.22 and Sobolev identifications -> singular and molecular application derivations; Proposition 2.18 also contradicted by same example.
impact.scope: Materially central invalid derivation; not proof that all main rate statements are false.

correction.statement: Retain the actual supremum definition and prove application hypotheses directly or supply a valid replacement regularity argument.
correction.verification: One-way inclusion and restricted gamma=1 alternative verified analytically.
correction.limits: General fractional-gamma results and all multiplier hypotheses not repaired here.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed from the supremum-resolvent definition and Lemma 2.16. With K e_k=2^k e_k and x_k=2^(-k/2), x is square summable whereas K^(1/2)x is not. Dyadic splitting uniformly bounds each resolvent sum; finite truncations have unbounded fractional graph norms and bounded Favard norms. The proof takes a spectral-variable-dependent maximizer through an integral. Remark 2.17, Corollaries 2.19/2.22 and the stated Sobolev/application route expressly use this identification. The surviving forward inclusion does not supply the false reverse identification; rates require separate assessment.

problems.title: Missing cross-integer branch in Lemma 2.6 proof

source_claim.locator: PDF p.15, first case of Lemma 2.6 proof

assumptions: alpha=3/4, gamma=5/4 is admissible and has k_alpha=0,k_gamma=1

check.type: Exact counterexample to case implication and constructive missing-case proof
steps: In Y=D(A^k), use increments of Ax of order b.
Double increment is bounded by s*t^b for s<=t and t*s^b for s>t.
Divide by s^a and take supremum to obtain t^(gamma-alpha).
check.result: Printed case division incomplete, claimed estimate recovered.

counterevidence: Direct proof supplies exactly the claimed exponent.

impact.dependency: Used in first commutator term of Theorem 2.8
impact.scope: Repairable proof omission, no independent theorem counterexample

independent_verification.result: Confirmed: gamma-alpha<1 does not imply equal integer parts (alpha=3/4,gamma=5/4). The stated double-increment repair splits s<=t and s>t and recovers t^(gamma-alpha), so the defect is confined to the displayed proof step rather than an established false lemma conclusion.

problems.title: Unitary phases omitted in displayed splitting formulas

source_claim.text: Potential factors are printed with real exponent tV/n or tQ^2/n rather than the unitary phase used by the surrounding result.

assumptions: Intended self-adjoint unitary dynamics and initial data in D(P^2+Q^2)

steps: Theorem 3.18 statement omits i while same-page proof explicitly uses exp(itQ^2/n).
A real growing exp(hQ^2) is not defined on every D(N) vector: psi proportional to (1+x^2)^(-2) belongs to D(N) but exp(hx^2)psi is not L^2 for h>0.

counterevidence: Same-page proof explicitly has intended unitary factors.
Gaussian calculation agrees with the intended O(h^2) local error.

impact.scope: Correctable formula errors; not a counterexample to intended unitary estimate

correction.statement: Use exp(-itV/n) with joint exp(-itH) in (3.43)-(3.44), and exp(itQ^2/n) in (3.45).
correction.verification: Matches proof and intended generator signs.
correction.limits: Complete Section 3 proof not independently certified.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed from equations 3.43-3.45 and their adjacent proofs. The potential factors omit the imaginary unit while the proof uses unitary phases. The literal real exponential can leave L2 on vectors in D(N); restoring the unitary phase is fixed by the surrounding derivation, limiting the verified defect.

positive_checks.evidence: Exact overlap e^(-ih)/sqrt(1-2ih-2h^2), leading norm error sqrt(2)h^2. Analytic check in report; native scalar evaluation retained separately.
positive_checks.scope: One smooth vector, not full numerical reproduction.

focused_acceptance_summary.scope: Focused acceptance of the three existing Problems: the Favard-space equivalence and its cited application chain, the cross-integer increment argument, and missing unitary phases. The dyadic counterexample, actual assumptions, surviving inclusions and stated repair limits were independently checked; no full-paper or new numerical convergence audit.
focused_acceptance_summary.assessment_review: Retain overall Major for the invalid Favard identification used in central derivations. Retain Minor for the repairable cross-integer proof case and explicit missing phases. No inference that every rate, the Coulomb rate or all operator results are false.
